summary: This document specified how to carry an H.263 video bitstream inside RTP packets. It was standards-track and is now historic.

eli5.summary: Cutting a video into small pieces and putting each into an envelope for the Internet.

questions: how is h.263 video carried in rtp
what are h.263 payload header modes a b and c
what is a gob in h.263
subtitle: How to slice an H.263 video stream into RTP packets so a receiver can keep decoding after a packet is lost.

tldr.problem: H.263 video has coding options and dependencies that make it hard to split into network packets and still decode the pieces that arrive when others are lost.
tldr.mechanism: Each RTP packet carries one H.263 video packet behind a payload header in one of three modes (A, B or C), which repeats the frame-level information a decoder needs.
tldr.outcome: Receivers can resynchronize after loss, best of all with mode A, but the scheme applies only to the 1996 version of H.263. This RFC is marked Historic.

today: RFC 2190 is marked Historic and no replacement is named in its metadata. It covers only the 1996 version of H.263.

sections.title: Putting H.263 into RTP
sections.content:
RFC 2190 describes a scheme to packetize an H.263 video stream for transport over RTP (RFC 1889). H.263 is defined by ITU-T Recommendation H.263 for video coding at very low data rates. RTP provides end-to-end transport functions for real-time data over multicast or unicast networks.

The H.263 bitstream is carried in the RTP payload without alteration, including the picture start code and the entire picture header. The RFC does not add the framing of H.223, so multiplexing audio and video in one packet is not accommodated. UDP and RTP already provide a more efficient way to multiplex.
sections.eli5: The video is put into envelopes exactly as it is, with nothing changed. Sound goes in its own separate envelopes.

sections.title: Design Issues with H.263
sections.content:
H.263 is based on H.261 but differs in ways that matter for packetizing. It has four negotiable coding options: Advanced Prediction, PB-frames, Syntax-based Arithmetic Coding and Unrestricted Motion Vectors. Each makes recovery from packet loss harder in some way, so their use is signaled in the payload header.

Pictures are split into groups of blocks (GOBs), and each GOB into macroblocks (MBs). A GOB header is optional. Without one, motion vectors may depend on the previous GOB, so a lost packet can make later data undecodable. Copying all those vectors into every packet would cost too much bandwidth, so the RFC strongly recommends a GOB header for every GOB at the start of a packet.

Some dependencies cannot be fixed this way, such as those in 4CIF and 16CIF pictures where a GOB spans more than one row of MBs, or with overlapped block motion compensation. Implementations should take these limits into account.
sections.eli5: Some comic pages only make sense if you saw the page before. So each envelope should start with a clear title, and the RFC warns that a few pages still depend on earlier ones.

sections.title: RTP Header Usage
sections.content:
Each packet is an RTP fixed header, then the H.263 payload header, then the H.263 bitstream. Each RTP packet carries only one H.263 video packet.

  • The M (marker) bit is 1 when the packet carries the end of the current frame, otherwise 0.
  • The payload type uses the value set by the RTP profile in use, for example RFC 1890.
  • The timestamp is the sampling instant of the frame, on a 90 kHz clock. It may be the same on successive packets if a frame fills more than one packet.
sections.eli5: Each envelope has a flag saying "this is the last piece of the picture" and a clock time so pieces of the same picture can be put together.

sections.title: The Three Payload Header Modes
sections.content:
The payload header comes in three formats, picked by the F and P bits. Mode A (F=0) is 4 bytes and allows fragmentation at GOB boundaries. Mode B (F=1, P=0) is 8 bytes and allows fragmentation at macroblock boundaries without PB-frames. Mode C (F=1, P=1) is 12 bytes and allows macroblock fragmentation with PB-frames.

All three carry fields such as SBIT and EBIT (bits to ignore in the first and last byte), SRC (source format) and flags I, U, S and A for the coding type and optional features. Modes B and C add QUANT, GOBN, MBA (the address of the first macroblock) and motion vector predictors, because the macroblock address is not otherwise coded in H.263.

Packets of different modes can be intermixed. Clients must be able to receive any mode, but decoding mode C is optional because PB-frames are optional.
sections.eli5: There are a short, a medium and a long label for the envelopes. The short one is used when you cut between big sections, and the longer ones when you have to cut in the middle of a section and need to say exactly where.

sections.title: Choosing a Mode and Limits
sections.content:
Mode A must be used for packets starting at a GOB or the picture start code. Mode B or C must be used whenever a packet has to start at a macroblock boundary, which is needed for GOBs larger than the network packet size.

The RFC strongly recommends mode A whenever possible. Its header is smaller, which saves overhead at very low data rates or small packet sizes, and a decoder can recover its state at GOB boundaries instead of having to synchronize with macroblocks.

The scheme applies to the 1996 version of H.263 and may not apply to bitstreams with features added afterwards. On security, the RFC says issues are addressed by RTP and that this memo adds no additional issues.
sections.eli5: Use the short label whenever you can. It is lighter, and it makes it easier to pick up where you left off after a lost piece.

fields.name: SBIT
fields.desc: Most significant bits to ignore in the first data byte.

fields.name: EBIT
fields.desc: Least significant bits to ignore in the last data byte.

fields.name: SRC
fields.desc: Source format, the resolution of the picture.

fields.name: DBQ
fields.desc: Differential quantization for the B frame.

fields.name: TRB
fields.desc: Temporal reference for the B frame.

fields.name: TR
fields.desc: Temporal reference for the P frame.
